picks.headline: AI debate has shifted from 'can we' to 'should we', IPG Autumn Conference 2026 hears
picks.excerpt: AI dominated the Independent Publishers Guild Autumn Conference, with new IPG research showing adoption among indie publishers has jumped to 76% in 2026 from 42% in 2023, and 72.9% now hold a formal AI policy. The report's blunt finding: AI may have damaged trust between publishers and authors more than it has actually changed workflows.
picks.rationale: Fresh hard numbers on where indie publishing actually stands on AI adoption and policy — a benchmark anyone writing an AI policy can measure against.

picks.headline: Oxford University Press updates guidelines as AI use 'measurably' under-disclosed
picks.excerpt: An OUP survey found a wide gap between how often researchers actually use AI in their writing and how often they declare it, prompting the publisher to rewrite its author submission guidelines. The update pushes disclosure of AI assistance from optional courtesy toward an explicit condition of submission.
picks.rationale: A major publisher turning AI disclosure into a submission requirement changes what authors must write down before they submit tomorrow.

picks.headline: Writers' AI Fears Often Run Ahead of the Facts
picks.excerpt: Friedman takes on three of the loudest writer anxieties — agents secretly using AI, detector false positives, and proving human authorship — and finds the online panic bears little resemblance to agency and publisher practice. She notes rejections tied to detection scores generally start around 20-25%, not at a light AI touch.
picks.rationale: Puts concrete thresholds and real agency practice behind the detector panic, so writers can calibrate instead of guessing.

picks.headline: Simon & Schuster is making indie publishing easier
picks.excerpt: Simon & Schuster relaunched Pocket Books for print deals and added Simon Stream with 50% net e-book royalties, aimed at self-published authors who want a major imprint's stamp. The pitch is explicitly positioned as a way for real books to stand out from the flood of AI-generated slop.
picks.rationale: A concrete new route and royalty rate for self-published authors, framed as a human-authorship signal against AI slop.

picks.headline: What Webtoon's New AI Partnership Could Mean for Translators
picks.excerpt: Webtoon is rolling out AI auto-translation for self-published Canvas creators plus 'byUS', a Korea-only interactive story-chat service that lets readers generate new stories from existing webcomics. Translators interviewed say the tooling can speed localization but still misses the cultural nuance that East Asian comics depend on.
picks.rationale: A shipping AI localization pipeline on a major creator platform, with working translators saying exactly where it breaks.
